$comment: What each fixture isolates, and what the Resolver must get right about it. Written before the Resolver exists, so it reads as a specification rather than a description of whatever the extractor happens to do.

design.handWritten: Not sampled from a real repository. The Phase A corpus was two JHipster-generated components, and generated code is far more regular than hand-written code -- schema fields derived from it inherit that bias (3_PhaseAFindings.md F5a). These are written to isolate one construct each instead.
design.pairs: Fixtures come in pairs that express the SAME semantics in different syntax. The pair is the assertion: both members must extract to equivalent output, differing only in the field that records which syntax was used. This is the check that catches D3's silent-failure mode -- a regex-based extractor tends to handle one member of a pair and quietly mis-handle the other, producing confidently wrong metadata rather than an error.

fixtures.isolates: How the public API is declared: @Input/@Output decorators versus the input()/output()/model() functions.
mustExtract: three inputs in both members, named label, count, internalName
count is required in both -- via the decorator option in one, input.required in the other
internalName carries alias 'aliasedName' in both
one output named changed with payload type number
declarationStyle is the ONLY field that may differ: 'decorator' versus 'signal'
the signal member additionally declares model:selected, which has no decorator equivalent

fixtures.isolates: How dependencies are injected: constructor parameters versus inject() field initializers.
mustExtract: three dependencies in both, named http, route, cache
visibility preserved: http private, route protected, cache private
cache carries optional and skipSelf modifiers in both -- as parameter decorators in one, as an options object in the other
resolvedUnitId is null for the two Angular tokens and non-null for CacheService
injectionStyle is the only field that may differ
the inject() member's dependencies are field initializers, so their loc is a field, not a constructor parameter

fixtures.isolates: Template control flow: structural directives (*ngIf/*ngFor/ngSwitch) versus block syntax (@if/@for/@switch).
mustExtract: one conditional, one loop, one switch with two cases, in both
the loop's track expression: trackBy function in one, track item.id in the other
the index alias in both
the else branch in both -- an ng-template reference in one, an @else block in the other
the block member additionally declares an @empty branch, which has no structural-directive equivalent
the uppercase pipe recorded once per member
construct is the only field that may differ

fixtures.isolates: Form construction: FormBuilder groups versus ngModel bindings.
mustExtract: approach is 'reactive' versus 'template-driven'
an email control with required and email validators in both
the reactive member's id control is disabled AND required -- the required rule is inert because disabled controls skip validation, and this must be visible in the output rather than collapsed
getRawValue() is recorded distinctly from value(): it includes disabled controls, which is load-bearing
the template-driven member has no form group id, so form:<name> ids are absent rather than invented

fixtures.isolates: Subscription teardown: takeUntilDestroyed versus a Subscription field unsubscribed in ngOnDestroy.
mustExtract: cleanupStrategy is 'takeUntilDestroyed' versus 'ngOnDestroy-unsubscribe'
leakRisk is 'none' for both -- neither leaks, by different means
the manual member implements OnDestroy and the other does not
the rxjs operator chain in both: map, plus takeUntilDestroyed in the first
an extractor that equates 'has ngOnDestroy' with 'safe' would pass the manual member and wrongly flag the other

notCoveredYet.$comment: Named so their absence is a decision rather than an oversight. Each is a construct the Phase A corpus exercised or the taxonomy names, with no fixture yet.
constructs: ViewChild/ContentChild queries, decorator and signal forms
inherited members from a base class -- the extensionPoints case (F5a)
cross-component shared mutable service state, which is the highest-severity migration risk and not observable from one unit (F3)
